DILG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA cor- Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City wvwvv dilg.gov.ph DILG OPINION No. 121 s. 2021 OCT 28 2021 PB RODULFO J. JUMAMOY Barangay Poblacion, Municipality of Ibanga, Bohol Dear PB Jumanoy: This has reference to your letter dated August IO, 2020 requesting for the Department's legal opinion on the following: ii. Can a member of the Sangguinang Barangay found guilty under Republic Act 9165 or the Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002 automatically return and/or reassume his position pending full compliance and completion of the condition imposed by the court decision based on the plea bargaining agreement and before the service of their remaining sentence beyond the credited period of confinement? In the absence of any specific pronouncement of accessory penalty/ies in the court decision itself, what are the administrative implications and/or legal consequences of the guilty decision against the barangay kagawad concern? Your first query, based on the letter, was grounded on the fact that the Joint Decision of the Regional Trial Court Branch 4 of Bohol did not discuss the matter regarding the return and/or re-assumption of the member of the Sangguinang Barangay of his position pending full compliance and completion of the condition imposed by the court. Based on the Joint Decision of the Regional Trial Court, Sangguniang Barangay Member Alvarado Butlig Jr. was found guilty beyond reasonable doubt for the offense of violation of Section 12, Article II of R.A. 9165 or the Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002 (Possession Drug Paraphernalia) and was imposed a straight penalty of imprisonment of One (1) Year and a fine of Ten Thousand Pesos (PIO,OOO.OO). Further, the Honorable Court imposed a condition to the said Sangguniang Barangay Member, to wit: "The consideration and admission of the plea bargaining agreement is subject to a condition that both accused should undergo a Drug Dependency Examination (DDE) to determine the extent of the accused's drug use. If the level of drug dependency is only slight or moderate, the accused shall be referred to a community based rehabilitation program, otherwise, if the drug dependency is serious, he shall be committed to a duly accredited drug rehabilitation center for a

minimum period of six (6) months from date of first confinement. The period of confinement shall be credited to the penalty as imposed herein if still unserved." (Emphasis supplied) The Honorable Court specifically imposed a penalty of one (I) year imprisonment with the condition that Sangguniang Barangay Member Butlig shall undergo a drug rehabilitation process, and that the rehabilitation confinement shall be credited to the penalty as imposed if still unserved In the case of People ofthe Philippines vs. Jalosjosl, the Supreme Court has ruled that: "More explicitly, 'imprisonment' in its general sense, is the restraint of one's liberty. As a punishment, it is restraint by judgment of a court or lawful tribunal, and is personal to the accused. The term refers to the restraint on the personal liberty of another; any prevention of his movements from place to place, or of his free action according to his own pleasure and will. Imprisonment is the detention of another against his will depriving him of his power of locomotion and it '[is] something more than mere loss of freedom. It includes the notion of restraint within limits defined by wall or any exterior barrier. ' It can be seen from the foregoing that incarceration, by its nature, changes an individual's status in society. Prison officials have the difficult and often thankless job of preserving the security in a potentially explosive setting, as well as of attempting to provide rehabilitation that prepares inmates for re-entry into the social mainstream. Necessarily, both these demands require the curtailment and elimination of certain rights." From the said ruling, it can be concluded that a convicted person or a public official imposed with a penalty of imprisonment cannot exercise certain rights as a result of the said penalty. The curtailment and elimination of certain rights includes the retum and/or re-assumption of the Sangguniang Barangay Member of his position. Assuming that Sangguniang Barangay Member Butlig has not yet complied with the conditions of the Honorable Court to undergo drug rehabilitation process, he cannot return to his position as an elective official as it will constitute as failure to serve his imposed sentence of one (1) year imprisonment as there will be no confinement to be credited to the penalty as imposed, if still unserved, so to speak. In other words, Sangguniang Barangay member Butlig has yet to serve his sentence imposed by the Honorable Court if he has not yet complied with the said conditions. The performance of legitimate and even essential duties by public officers has never been an excuse to free a person validly in prison.2 The functions and duties of the office are not substantial distinctions which lift him from the class of prisoners interrupted in their freedom and restricted in liberty of movement.3 Sangguniang Barangay Member 1 G.R. NOS. 132875-76 February 3, 2000. 2 ld. 3 ld.

Butlig has to comply with the conditions set by the Honorable Court before he can reassume his position as Sangguniang Barangay Member. As to the second query, the Department is of the opinion that an administrative case against the convicted elective barangay official may be filed before the sangguniang panlungsod or sangguniang bayan concerned based on the grounds specified under Section 60 of the Local Government Code. Section 60 of the LGC provides, to wit: SECTION 60. Grounds for Disciplinary Actions. — An elective local official may be disciplined, suspended, or removed from office on any of the following grounds: xxxx xxxx xxxx (d) Commission of any offense involving moral turpitude or an offense punishable by at least prision mayor; xxxx xxxx xxxx (h) Such other grounds as may be provided in this Code and other laws. An elective local official may be removed from office on the grounds enumerated above by order of the proper court. However, please take note that the Supreme Court explained in the case of Civil Service Commission vs. Belagan4, in order to constitute an administrative offense, misconduct should relate to or be connected with the performance of the official functions and duties of a public officer. Further, in the case of Baterina vs. HRET5, the Supreme Court ruled that moral turpitude implies something 'immoral in itself, regardless of the fact that it is punishable by law or not. It must not merely be mala prohibita (wrong because prohibited), but the act itself must inherently be immoral. The doing of the act itself, and not its prohibition by statute, fixes the moral turpitude. Apropos thereto, the mere possession of a prohibited drug cannot be considered immoral by itself if it were not punishable by law, much like illegal possession of a deadly weapon and incidental participation of illegal recruitment.6 Considering that Sangguniang Barangay Member Butlig was convicted of Section 12, Article II of R.A. 9165 (Possession of Drug Paraphernalia), such offense does not involve moral turpitude. Further, the conviction of his crime does not carry a penalty of prision mayor. Hence, Sangguniang Barangay Member Butlig cannot be disciplined, suspended or removed based on Section 60 (d) of the Local Government Code of 1991. G.R. NO. 132164, October 19, 2004. 5 G.R NO. 210303, April 21, 2015.

As to the Sections 39 and 40 of the Local Government Code of 1991 , it explicitly pertains to qualifications and disqualifications in election of a local elective official which is not the issue at hand. Once elected, these disqualifications cited do not apply to elected local officials. However, note that under Section 40, the penalty of removal from office as a result of an administrative case shall be a bar to the candidacy of the respondent for any elective local office. This opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities and the courts. We hope to have assisted you accordingly. Thank you. Very trul AUTHORITY OF B. DINO MA HE SECRETARY: d secretary for Barangay Affairs cc: Dir. Leocadio T. Trovela Regional Director, DILG-Region VII Sudlod, Lahug, Cebu City
